lens.reason: Two blind same-model lanes are the OW-19 floor; a third lens is added because two of the three severe axes (ecclesial contestedness, connections) bear directly on row prose, and the reception-tradition lens is the one most likely to catch a neutrality breach (rule 7) in the densest divided-reading rows (11:2-11:34, 14:33-14:36, 12:1-14:40). All lanes run on claude-opus-5-5 under OW-25, so model-family decorrelation is unavailable; the third lens is decorrelated by KIND only, and a 2-1 split between same-family lanes is not a majority.

scrutiny_targets.target: 8:1-11:1 idol-food argument with the ch 9 digression
scrutiny_targets.disposition: Region A: one parent P07 8:1-11:1; rows may open at 9:1, 10:1, 10:14, 10:23, 10:31 but each discloses its place in the idol-food argument; ch 9 is never a parent; 11:1 closes backward (lexical echo with 10:33). Expected grades: parent A, 9:1 and 10:1 row seams B, 11:1/11:2 A.

scrutiny_targets.target: 12:1-14:40 with ch 13 inset and 14:33b-36 text-critical block
scrutiny_targets.disposition: Region B: one parent P10 12:1-14:40; ch 13 is a row-level inset bracketed by the repeated imperative at 12:31 and 14:1; 14:33b-36 handled as a contested-attachment row with the transposition as metadata only. Expected grades: parent A, 12:31 attachment C, 14:33/14:34 C, 14:36/14:37 B.

Region C: two parents P08 11:2-11:16 and P09 11:17-11:34 on the praise / negated-praise pair; the Supper tradition 11:23-11:26 stays in one row with its application 11:27-11:34. Expected grades: 11:16/11:17 A, 11:22/11:23 B, no row seam at 11:26/11:27.

Region D: one parent P11 15:1-15:58; creed 15:3-15:7 with 15:8-15:11 in one row; candidate row onsets 15:12, 15:20, 15:29, 15:35, 15:50 or 15:51, 15:58. Expected grades: parent A, creed row 15:1-15:11 A, 15:57-15:58 close A, 15:50 versus 15:51 C, others B.

Region E: slogan extent convention stated (§10 C3); slogan and response never split; WEB quotation marks measured and excluded; 6:13 (second slogan), 7:1, 8:1, 8:4, 8:8 flagged contested-extent. Expected grade per slogan row B, extent disclosure mandatory.

Region F: two parents P05 7:1-7:24 and P06 7:25-7:40 on the 7:25 peri de heading and the calling refrain; 7:8, 7:10, 7:12 addressee series and 7:36 are row-level candidates. Expected grades: 7:24/7:25 A, 7:1 A, 7:8 B, 7:10 B, 7:12 B, 7:36 B.

Region G: two parents P12 16:1-16:18 and P13 16:19-16:24; 16:12 peri de is a row onset, not a parent seam; maranatha quoted from RP with the SBL division disclosed. Expected grades: 15:58/16:1 A, 16:18/16:19 B (frame edge to Fable), 16:12 B.

device_review_items.disposition: Ruling D1: a peri de onset rests on the formula, not on the edition's sentence punctuation; sentence_start is recorded as edition-dependent and never decides a seam.

Ruling D4: vocative ἀδελφοί never sets a boundary alone; it corroborates only beside another tier-1 signal; non-vocative uses (e.g. the articular nominative at 9:5 and 16:20) carry no boundary weight.

Witness discipline: on the ten disagreement verses rows quote RP and disclose the SBL wording when the row's argument rests on the hit (10:23 μοι, 16:24 Amen, 1:14 thanksgiving phrase, 10:1, 11:2 and the rest).

device_review_items.item: calendar references in the closing chapter
device_review_items.disposition: No calendar onset rule; 5:7, 16:2, 16:8 are metadata in the rows that hold them; recorded in cal_no_onset and listed for Fable.
Maranatha is quoted from RP in Greek script with the SBL word division disclosed; classed for now as a language-switch object inside the closing frame, not as an onset; class to Fable.
Ruling D7: thanksgiving verbs at 1:14, 10:30, 14:18 (and the 14:16 amen) are texture, not frame and not onsets.
Ruling D8: frame parents P01 1:1-1:9 and P13 16:19-16:24 adopted on the orchestrator's edges; the rival closing edge 16:13 is recorded in §7 G and sent to Fable.
Recorded in the lens record: every role runs on claude-opus-5-5 (OW-25 grader_fallback); lens decorrelation is by kind only.

cal_no_onset.rule: No calendar onset rule for 1 Corinthians: no month-plus-day date exists (EXTRACTED, device inventory year_word 0, month_word 0); the calendar references at 5:7 (pascha), 16:2 (first of the week) and 16:8 (Pentecost) are metadata in their rows and never open a row by themselves.
